Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The umpires are out in the middle and so are the Australian players. Rohit Sharma and Shubman Gill are the openers for India. Mitchell Starc has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
... The Run Chase ...

Right then, 270 runs needed for India to win and seal the series. The target is not a big one considering the pitch conditions and spin might not even play a big role during the chase but the batting has let India down so far which gives Australia more than half a chance to get the win. Let's see if India can turn up well and clinch the series by chasing this down. The run chase is coming up soon.

The Aussies started off with flying colors but Hardik Pandya changed the momentum and shifted that in favor of India. The hosts controlled the middle phase as well with the spinners bossing play. For India, Hardik Pandya and Kuldeep Yadav were their best bowlers as they scalped 3 wickets each. They were well supported by Axar Patel and Mohammed Siraj who took a couple of wickets each and overall, India will be pretty content with that effort.

After winning the toss and electing to bat, the Aussies started off sensationally as the two openers came out with a positive mindset and scored at a blistering pace. The duo of Mitchell Marsh and Travis Head scored 68 for the first wicket but the middle order failed to capitalize on a brilliant platform laid by the openers. The introduction of Hardik Pandya into the attack helped the hosts as he changed the game by scalping 3 wickets in quick succession. The lower middle order along with the tail then scored some crucial runs and helped the Aussies to post a total they could fight for. Most of the Aussie batters did get starts but no one could step up and convert that into a big one.

A good fightback from India after a difficult start right at the top restricts Australia to a total of 269 runs for the loss of 10 wickets. Inspired bowling changes and a clinical fielding performance helps India to restrict the Aussies for not too many on the board in this series decider.

OUT! CAUGHT! This time Mitchell Starc finds the man in the deep. Mohammed Siraj bangs it in short again and over middle and leg. Mitchell Starc looks to take on the pull shot again and hits it aerial but flat. The ball goes toward deep mid-wicket where Ravindra Jadeja takes a good catch low in front of him. Siraj finishes things off with his second wicket and Australia have been bowled out for 269 runs in 49 overs!
Commentary.Howout: c Ravindra Jadeja b Mohammed Siraj

Commentary.Commentary: Leg bye! Good length on the pads, Adam Zampa hops back and looks to work it away but misses. The ball goes off the pads and just behind square leg as the batters pick up a leg bye.
On a length and around leg stump, Starc works it away through mid-wicket for one.
Slower one, on a good length around off and going away. Mitchell Starc looks to play it late but is well beaten.
SIX! Well struck! Banged in short and over leg stump, Mitchell Starc stands tall and pulls it just over Ravindra Jadeja on the mid-wicket fence for a maximum.
Fuller in length and just angling across off, Mitchell Starc hangs deep and mistimes the heave toward mid-wicket.
Good length angling into the legs, Adam Zampa nudges it away in front of square on the leg side and picks up a couple of runs.
Pitched up on off stump, blocked out.
Good length, pushed wider of the off stump and nipping it away, Adam Zampa loosely throws his hands at it and is beaten on the outside edge.
Length ball around the top of off, blocked out.
FOUR! Full and on the pads, Adam Zampa gets inside the line and just helps it down to fine leg for a boundary.
On a good length, slanting it into the body, worked away past square leg for a single.
Hard length, angled in from around off, Adam Zampa hops and looks to block but misses and gets hit high on the pads.

Short of a length over off stump, Adam Zampa pulls this one toward deep square leg and picks up a couple of runs. Good effort from Shubman Gill in the deep as he ran from deep mid-wicket and dived in to save two runs.
Leg bye! This is banged in short and around leg stump, Mitchell Starc looks to swivel and pull but misses. The ball goes off the body toward backward square leg and they get a leg bye.
Pitched up outside off, Adam Zampa presses forward and caresses it through the cover region for one.
Very full on middle and leg, driven down to long on for a single.
Hardik Pandya comes back on and starts off with a length ball on off stump. Mitchell Starc defends it out toward cover.
Goes wider of the crease and angles in a fuller delivery from outside off, Adam Zampa looks to block but is well beaten.
Leg bye! Full and down leg, Mitchell Starc looks to flick but misses. The ball goes off the pads and KL Rahul does well to dive to his right and get a glove on it. They scamper through for a leg bye.
Good length around the pads, worked away past square leg for a single.
Adam Zampa walks out last in the middle.

OUT! CAUGHT! Straight to the man and Australia on the verge of being bowled out. Mohammed Siraj bowls a heavy delivery and bangs it in over middle. Ashton Agar just looks to take it on but ends up flat-batting it toward deep mid-wicket. There's no a lot of power on the shot and it is an easy catch for Axar Patel in the deep.
Commentary.Howout: c Axar Patel b Mohammed Siraj

Commentary.Commentary: Comes from around the wicket now and bowls it full around off, Mitchell Starc drives it straight back past the bowler for a single.
Length ball, slanted across the left-hander, Ashton Agar taps it toward deep cover for a single.
Mitchell Starc is the next man in.

OUT! BOWLED'EM UP! You miss I hit stuff as Axar Patel lands one fractionally short and in the line of stumps, Sean Abbott goes for a big heave and misses out only to see the stumps being clattered by the ball.
Quicker and flatter around middle, Sean Abbott slices this to point.
short in length around middle, Ashton Agar tucks this to deep mid-wicket for a single.
SIX! This time it is Ashton Agar. Over-pitched on off, Ashton Agar stands and lofts this over the long on fielder for a maximum.
Fuller around middle, Sean Abbott pushes this to sweeper cover for a single.
SIX! That's a huge hit for six. Fuller and in the slot for Sean Abbott, he clears his front leg and smashes this way over the fence at long on for half-a-dozen runs.
Axar Patel (7-0-43-1) is back on.
Bouncer wide of off, Ashton Agar toe pokes this to point for no run.
Short-pitched delivery head high, Ashton Agar pulls this just short of Rohit Sharma at short mid-wicket. A good effort but the ball lands in front of the Indian skipper.
On a length in middle, Sean Abbott pulls this to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Back of a length around middle, Sean Abbott defends this to short mid-wicket for no run.
On a length around pads, Ashton Agar rolls this to long on for a single.
Good length delivery on pads, Ashton Agar works this to short mid-wicket for no run.
Fuller and in middle, Ashton Agar pushes this to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Sharp turn as he floats one on off, Ashton Agar could do nothing and gets beaten on his outside edge.
Short in length wide of off, Sean Abbott punches this of the back foot to sweeper cover for a single.

There is a slight halt in the play as there is a dog running onn the ground. The batters are rehydrating themselves out in the middle due to the warm conditions as well. In general, it has been slow going even with the spinners bowling a lot of overs. It is all sorted now and play can continue.
FOUR! Confident stroke for four. Top-spinner from around the wicket, Sean Abbott plays the reverse sweep and smashes a boundary toward third man.
Tossed up in middle, Ashton Agar pushes this to long on for a single.
Tossed up on pads, Ashton Agar has flicked this towards deep mid-wicket for a couple.
Fuller and in middle, Sean Abbott drills this down the ground for a couple. Mohammed Siraj fields well running in from long on to save this going over the fence.
Back of a length over the off-stump line, Sean Abbott looks for the big heave on the on side but misses out.
Yorker nailed to perfection. Sean Abbott keeps this out.
FOUR! Thrashed for four. On a length outside off, Sean Abbott stands tall and plays the back foot drives in the gap at cover for a boundary.
On a length around middle, Sean Abbott defends this off the back foot.
Short and wide outside off, Ashton Agar cuts this wide of third man for a single.
Quicker and flatter in middle, Sean Abbott rolls this back to the bowler.
Fuller and turning from middle, Ashton Agar drills this past the bowler for a single.
Short in length around middle, Sean Abbott tucks this to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Fuller and wide of off, Sean Abbott pokes and this and gets an inside edge to short mid-wicket.
Fuller one on off, Sean Abbott defends this to short cover.
Tossed up on off, Sean Abbott looks to sweep and manages a top edge over the keeper's head for a couple.
Length ball on off stump, kept out on the on-side by Agar.
Banged in short and over off stump, Ashton Agar gets on top of the bounce and pulls it toward mid-wicket. Rohit Sharma there misfields and concedes a couple of runs.
On as hard length, angling in from outside off, Sean Abbott punches it toward cover-point where Rohit Sharma makes a half-stop and the batters scamper through for the single.
Length ball, right on the money this time, Sean Abbott blocks it out on the leg side.
WIDE! Goes wider of the crease again and spills this one down leg, left alone for a wide.
Bowled from wider of the crease and angling it in, Sean Abbott shuffles and works it away past square leg for a couple of runs.
Good length around middle, angling in, kept out by Sean Abbott.

One review that was for just the bowler's satisfaction. Kuldeep Yadav floats this one up nicely around off turning it in. Ashton Agar leans on looking to block but misses and gets hit on the pads. There is a loud appeal for lbw but it is turned down and he wants the review. Rohit Sharma disagrees at first but then goes for it and Ball Tracking confirms the impact is well outside the line of leg stump.
Tossed up on off stump, Ashton Agar blocks it off the front foot.
Here comes the googly now! Flatter one around off stump, turning in sharply, Ashton Agar goes on the back foot to keep this out.
Nicely floated up on middle and leg and gets it to turn away from the left-hander. Ashton Agar manages to keep it out.
Short and around off, this is pushed off the back foot toward the bowler.
Ashton Agar walks out in the middle.

OUT! TIMBER! Kuldeep Yadav comes back on and gets rid of Alex Carey with a gem of a delivery. Kuldeep comes from over the wicket and bowls this one flatter around leg stump. The length is shortened and the ball just turns away sharply off the deck. Alex Carey stays back shaping up to play the sweep but gets caught on the crease and even after he tries to adjust and get some bat on it, the ball goes past the outside edge and into the stumps. Australia in deep trouble now.
Length ball, angling across the left-hander, this is sliced down to third man for a run.
Back of a length over middle, Alex Carey tries to pull off the back foot but hits it uppishly wide of the man at mid on.
Good length, outside the off stump, Sean Abbott stays back and taps it in front of point for a single.
Pitched up around off, this is hit uppishly as well, well wide of cover-point and for a single down to sweeper cover.

FOUR! Uppish but safe! Good length angled across the off stump, Alex Carey drives it but off the outer half and past a diving Suryakumar Yadav at cover-point for a boundary. The 200 is now up for Australia.
Length ball on off stump, Alex Carey defends it off the front foot.
Sean Abbott walks out next in the middle. Hardik Pandya (4-0-20-3) comes back into the attack.

OUT! CAUGHT! Marcus Stoinis gives his wicket away and he will be highly disappointed with that. Axar Patel fires this one in at 95.5 clicks and onto middle and leg. Stoinis backs away and frees his arms before trying to smoke it over the long on fence. The ball comes off the toe end of the bat and goes toward wide long on. Shubman Gill there runs to his right and takes a good catch. India get a wicket against the run of play here.
Commentary.Howout: c Shubman Gill b Axar Patel

Commentary.Commentary: Angling into the pads, Alex Carey leans on and works it to wide long on for a run.
Flatter one, angled into the leg stump, Marcus Stoinis stays back and punches it down to long off for a single.
A tad shorter around off, holding in the pitch, Stoinis eases it toward point.
Floated up, a bit round arm and on middle and leg, Marcus Stoinis drives it straight to cover-point.
Quicker one, angled into middle and leg, Alex Carey backs away and cuts it through cover for a single.
On a length outside off, Alex Carey slices this to third man for a single to end the over.
Fuller and on pads, Marcus Stoinis tucks this to deep square leg for a single.
On a length around middle, Marcus Stoinis defends this off the front foot towards short cover.
FOUR! Overpitched around off, Marcus Stoinis drills this down the ground for a boundary towards long on.
Fuller around middle, Marcus Stoinis defends this.
On a good length around middle and angled in. Alex Carey tucks it into the vacant space around mid-wicket for a single.
Quicker one on the pads, worked away toward square leg for a single. 13 off the over, a good one for Australia.
SIX! A lapse in error on the field has cost India this boundary. Flighted ball on middle, Alex Carey makes room and hammers it away right back over the bowler's head for a maximum.

NO BALL! Floated up outside off, Marcus Stoinis drives it down to long off for a single. The umpire has called a no ball for the number of fielders inside the ring and not for the front foot. Nevertheless, it will be a Free Hit to follow.
Short again, this time Alex Carey backs away and cuts it towards deep point for a run.
Shortens the length and bowls it on off, kept out.
Quicker one at 97.2 clicks and outside off, slapped away in front of point for a single.
Flatter one around off, Marcus Stoinis taps it away behind point and races back for a couple of runs.
Shortish ball outside off, Alex Carey frees his arms and slaps it over the cover-point for a couple of runs.
Excellent length, right on the money and Alex Carey blocks it out.
Four dots on the trot now! Hard length, angling in from around middle, Carey fends it toward mid-wicket.
Short of a good length around off, Alex Carey with a short-arm jab toward mid on.
Pitched up around off, Alex Carey punches it toward mid off.

Mohammad Shami comes back and starts from around the wicket. This is bowled on a length and angling in from outside off. Alex Carey looks to drive but the ball stays low and beats him on the inside edge.
Quicker and flatter around off, blocked out.
Shorter in length and around middle, Alex Carey goes down to sweep but gets it off the gloves. The ball loops up over the keeper's head and they get a single.
Full and around off, Alex Carey looks to drive but gets an inside edge toward short fine leg.
Floated up around off, pushed off the front foot through extra cover for one.
FOUR! Nicely done! On middle, Marcus Stoinis gets down on one knee and plays the reverse paddle fine of the man at short third man and picks up a boundary.
Quicker one, sliding it into the legs, Alex Carey works it behind square leg for a single.
Flatter and around leg, this is worked off the back foot past mid-wicket for one.
Quicker one on off stump, Alex Carey presses forward to defend.
This is fired in around off stump, Marcus Stoinis pushes it firmly down to long off and picks up a run.
Fuller and outside off, driven straight to extra cover.
Beaten! Bowls it a bit wider of the off pole and Marcus Stoinis looks for the cover drive. The ball grips slightly and goes past the outside edge.
Flatter one on the pads, nudged away toward short fine leg for a single.

Floated up around leg, Marcus Stoinis strides out and pads it away. The ball loops up and Virat Kohli grabs it at leg slip and there is half an appeal for the catch, just to keep the crowd entertained perhaps.
FIVE WIDES! Beats everyone! Tossed up on leg stump and this one turns in sharply, going past the keeper and fine of the man at leg slip as well, the ball runs away into the fence.
Tosses it up around middle, Alex Carey drives it down to long off for a single.
Turning onto the pads, Marcus Stoinis tucks it away through backward square leg for one.
FOUR! Nicely done! Floated up on a length and spinning down leg, Marcus Stoinis plays the reverse paddle and gets it fine of short third man for a boundary.
Floats it up now outside off, Alex Carey heaves it to deep mid-wicket and collects a run.
Flatter trajectory on off stump, Alex Carey keeps it out on the off side.
Fuller around middle, Alex Carey milks this wide of square leg for a single.
Tossed up outside off, Marcus Stoinis slices this to sweeper cover for a single.
Short in length around pads, Alex Carey nudges this to deep square leg for a single.
Fuller around middle, Alex Carey defends this of the front foot.
Fuller outside off, Marcus Stoinis drives this to long off for a single.
Fuller around off, Marcus Stoinis pushes this to short cover for no run.
Tossed up around middle, Marcus Stoinis tucks this to square leg for a single.
Fuller around off, Marcus Stoinis punches this to short cover.
Fuller and quicker around pads, Alex Carey plays the reverse sweep to backward point for a single.
FOUR! Fuller outside off, Alex Carey leans ahead and sweeps this wide of fine leg fielder for a boundary.
Floated up on a length around off, Marcus Stoinis pushes it down to long off for a single.

Drinks break! The Indian spinners are not letting Australia get away one bit. After a three-wicket blitz by Hardik Pandya, Australia managed to build a steady stand courtesy of David Warner and Marnus Labuschagne but both have now disappeared and the visitors are in a heap of trouble. They need a stand now to take this inning deep and try to get to 250. Also, Marcus Stoinis walks out to bat now.

OUT! TAKEN IN THE DEEP! Tossed up outside off, Marnus Labuschagne advances down the track and looks to clear the long off fielder but the bat tilts in his hands and the ball has ballooned over the head of Shubman Gill at long off who makes no mistake and collects this with ease. Australia lose half of their side on a score of 138.
Commentary.Howout: c Shubman Gill b Kuldeep Yadav

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller outside off, Marnus Labuschagne gently slices this to the off side for a single.

FOUR! Innovation gets a boundary after some time for the Aussies. Fuller outside off, Marnus Labuschagne shuffles to his off and scoops this wide of Washington Sundar at short fine leg for a boundary. Sundar puts in a brilliant effort but fails to save the ball reaching the fence.
Fuller and on off, Alex Carey pushes this wide of Rohit Sharma at short cover for a quick single.
Fuller outside off, Marnus Labuschagne drives this to sweeper cover and rotates the strike.
Fuller and quicker on off, Marnus Labuschagne pushes this to point.
Short in length around pads, Alex Carey tucks this wide of short fine leg for a single.
Fuller and on off, Marnus Labuschagne blocks this out in front of him.
Quicker and flatter outside off, Marnus Labuschagne dabs this to short point.
Short in length outside off, Alex Carey pushes this to sweeper cover for a single.
Fuller around pads, Alex Carey pushes this to long on for a comfortable rotation of strike.
Tossed up outside off, Marnus Labuschagne drills this to long off for a single.
Fuller outside off, Marnus Labuschagne pushes this to cover-point.
Short in length around middle, Alex Carey pushes this straight to the fielder at short mid-wicket.
Tossed up around pads, Alex Carey tucks this and finds the fielder at short mid-wicket.
Fuller around middle, Alex Carey works this to short mid-wicket.
Quicker and fuller in middle, Marnus Labuschagne pushes this to long on for a single.
Tossed up in middle, Alex Carey tucks this to long on for a single.
Fuller and off, Alex Carey defends this off the front foot.
Fuller outside off, Alex Carey drills this to long off for a single as he gets off the mark.
Fuller around middle, Alex Carey pushes this back to the bowler.
Googly first up to Alex Carey, he strides out and looks to defend but gets beaten as the ball hits his pads. Rohit looked interested in going upstairs but the bowler refused.
Alex Carey walks out to bat now.

OUT! IN THE AIR AND TAKEN! Kuldeep Yadav gets his man. Leg-spinner on off, David Warner advances down the track to slog this out of the park but the ball holds a bit into the surface and it takes a leading edge towards long off. Hardik Pandya makes no mistake and takes a good running running towards the ball in front of him.
Commentary.Howout: c Hardik Pandya b Kuldeep Yadav

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller and on off, Marnus Labuschagne drills this to long off for a single.
Tossed up around middle, Marnus Labuschagne reverse sweeps this to the third man for a couple.
Tossed up in middle, Marnus Labuschagne pushes this to long on for a single.
Fuller around middle, Marnus Labuschagne defends this of the front foot.
Fuller around pads, Marnus Labuschagne edges this onto his pads and just falls in the vacant area at short leg.
Full and wide of off, Marnus Labuschagne strides forward and pushes this gently to point.
Quicker at a flatter trajectory on off, Marnus Labuschagne defends this staying in his crease.
Tossed up outside off, Marnus Labuschagne pushes this back to the bowler.
Fuller around pads, David Warner looks to flick but gets it clipped of his pads for no run.
Short in length on top of middle, Marnus Labuschagne pulls this towards deep square leg for a single.
Fuller around midle, Marnus Labuschagne defends this of the front foot.
SIX! Up in the air and just over the fence. Tossed up in middle, Marnus Labuschagne slog sweeps this but gets a leading edge that flies just over the fence at deep mid-wicket for a maximum.
Fuller with a bit more pace, Marnus Labuschagne guides this to point.
Short in length around off, David Warner smashes this off the back foot to long on for a single.
Fuller around middle, Marnus Labuschagne top edges this in front of the gully.
Short in length on pads, David Warner milks this wide of square leg for a single.
Fuller around middle, David Warner pushes this to square leg for no run.
Tossed up around pads, David Warner advances down the track and pushes this to short mid-wicket.
Fuller one around middle, David Warner tucks this to short mid-wicket.
Full and wide of off, David Warner pushes this to short cover.
Tossed up on pads, David Warner tucks this to short fine leg nd takes a single.
Quicker and on a flatter trajectory around middle, David Warner dabs this to point for no run.
Flighted on middle, David Warner gets on his back foot and defends this.
Fuller around middle, David Warner defends this of the front foot.
FOUR! Beautiful stroke for four. Tossed up on off, David Warner walks down the track and lofts this inside out over the fielder at cover for four.
Tossed up in middle, Marnus Labuschagne pushes this to long on for a single.

In the air...and, just short! Ravindra Jadeja drags this one down a bit around the leg stump. David Warner looks to pick it up off the back foot and loft it behind square but ends up getting a top edge. The ball goes up in the air and over backward square leg. Mohammed Siraj runs in from the deep and dives forward to his right, failing to reach it. The batters pick up a couple of runs as well.
Slightly flighted outside off, Labuschagne eases it down to long off and rotates the strike.
Drifted in and sliding onto the pads, Marnus Labuschagne fails to get it away.
Flatter delivery around off, tapped away toward cover.
Quicker one on the legs, David Warner goes deep in his crease and works it away 'round the corner for one.
Flatter delivery around off, this is knocked down through mid on for a single.
Drops it short and on the pads, Marnus Labuschagne flicks it off the back foot through mid-wicket for a run.
This is full and on off stump, Warner pushes it down to long off for a single. The 100 is now up for Australia.
Quicker and flatter through the air, turning away from the leg stump, David Warner looks to block but misses and gets hit on the pads.
Excellent running! Tossed up outside off, David Warner strokes it away toward sweeper cover and races back for the second.

A ripper of a delivery from Kuldeep Yadav! Tosses this one up on a length and on off stump, gripping and turning away sharply. David Warner leans on to defend but is beaten past the outside edge and the substitute keeper Ishan Kishan whips off the bails. The bowler and keeper appeal for stumping but the umpire says no and rightly so as the replays confirm Warner had his back leg inside the crease.
Tosses it up first up and floats it outside off, David Warner looks to drive through cover but mistimes it on the leg side.
This is angled into the stumps, Marnus Labuschagne defends it with soft hands.
A tad short and on the pads, David Warner works it off the back foot past square leg for one.
Pulls the length back and bowls it on middle, Labuschagne punches it down to long on for a run.
Drifted into middle and leg, Labuschagne blocks it out again.
Stump-to-stump bowling, blocked out by Labuschagne.
Bowled on middle, David Warner pushes it through mid on for a single.
Ishan Kishan has replaced KL Rahul behind the wickets as a substitute wicket-keeper for the moment.
Tossed up in middle, Marnus Labuschagne pushes this to long on for a single.
Good length around middle, angling in, Labuschagne just about defends it out.
Good length again, outside off, Marnus Labuschagne plays it down to short third man.
Good length around the pads, tucked away through mid-wicket for a single.
Back of a length around off, dabbed down to third man for a single.
Back of a length, angling in from outside off, Marnus Labuschagne looks to pull but is beaten past the inside edge.
Full and around off, Labuschagne drives it down to long off for a single.
Quicker and flatter, turning into the legs, David Warner goes on the back foot and works it past square leg for a run.
Floated up a bit outside off, Labuschagne drives it square of the wicket to deep cover-point for a single.
Quicker one, at 98 clicks and around off, Labuschagne pushes it toward cover.
Flatter again, angling onto middle, Labuschagne blocks it out.
Flatter one on off stump, Labuschagne looks to drive on the up but gets it nowhere.
WIDE! Drifted just down the leg side and a wide is signalled.
A well-directed short ball on the body. David Warner gets hurried on but manages to pull it away through backward square leg for a couple of runs.
Back of a length around off, Marnus Labuschagne eases it off the back foot through covers for a single.
Full and outside off, Marnus Labuschagne looks for the cover drive but mistimes it completely.
Marnus Labuschagne is the new man in.

OUT! DRAGGED ON! Hardik Pandya with his third wicket inside as many overs and Mitchell Marsh departs as well. Pandya bowls this on a fuller length in that channel around off and invites the drive. Marsh stays put and just reaches out for the cover drive. The feet don't move and the inside edge is found. The ball goes on to castle into the middle stump and Marsh departs 3 runs short of a half-century. Australia firmly pushed back at the moment.
FOUR! Banged in short and over middle, a comfortable height for the batter and Mitchell Marsh pulls it away behind square leg for a boundary.
Bowled on a good length around off, David Warner waits on the back foot and taps it behind point for a single.

Time for a Drinks break. Australia was well on top for the majority of the first hour or so but the dismissals of Travis Head and Steven Smith have brought India back into this game. This partnership becomes crucial for the visitors if they are to post a big total today. Interesting to see how David Warner bats at an unfamiliar no. 4 position for him.
Floated on the legs, Mitchell Marsh simply works it toward mid-wicket.
Drifted onto middle and leg, Mitchell Marsh plays it with soft hands toward cover.
Quicker one at the stumps, Mitchell Marsh keeps it out on the off side.
Fuller and on off stump, David Warner swings across the line and heaves it to wide long on for a run.
Flatter one around off, Mitchell Marsh eases it away toward sweeper cover for a single.
Starts off with a fullish delivery around the legs, David Warner pushes it through mid on and rotates the strike.
Ravindra Jadeja replaces Axar Patel.

Banged in short and over off stump, Mitchell Marsh decides to take it on and goes for the pull. Marsh pulls it away in between deep mid-wicket and long on but without much timing. Mohammed Siraj tries to run to his right from long on and get there but doesn't and the batters get a couple of runs.
Fullish length around off and angling across, David Warner pushes it off the outside edge and through backward point for a single.
On a good length around leg, David Warner gets cramped for room as he tucks it toward mid-wicket.
Pitches this one up as well, on the off stump, David Warner strokes it toward mid off.
David Warner walks out next in the middle.

OUT! EDGED AND GONE! Hardik Pandya strikes once again and Australia are now two down. This is pitched up in that channel around off and it is a scrambled-seam delivery. Steven Smith looks for the expansive cover drive and gets on the front foot to do so. Smith gets a big outside edge that carries through to the keeper and KL Rahul grabs it easily. Smith departs cheaply and Pandya has got India right back in.
Commentary.Howout: c KL Rahul b Hardik Pandya

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length around off, Steven Smith punches it out in front of cover.
Full and straight, blocked out.

Drops it short and outside off, Mitchell Marsh rocks back and cuts it away hard toward deep point. Mohammed Siraj runs around to his left from deep cover and saves a couple of runs but the replays show that Siraj's heel clipped the boundary rope as he was getting up and it will be a boundary. 2000 runs in ODIs for Mitchell Marsh!
This is speared in on the stumps, Marsh defends it out.

Brilliant fielding by Virat Kohli and for the second time in this game, he saves a certain boundary. Fraction shorter on off stump, crunched off the back foot by Mitchell Marsh to the left of short extra cover where Kohli makes the stop.
This is fired in a bit onto off and middle, Mitchell Marsh makes a solid block off the front foot.
Good running! Floated up around off, Mitchell Marsh drives it on the up through the cover region and picks up a couple of runs.
Back of a length around off, Steven Smith goes back and pushes it out on the off side.
Steven Smith walks out at no. 3.

OUT! CAUGHT! This time Hardik Pandya gets his man and Australia lose their first wicket. This is banged in short and wide by Pandya. Head goes chasing after it but doesn't move his feet. Travis Head slashes it away aerially wide of the man at third man. Kuldeep Yadav there runs to his left and takes a really sharp catch tumbling down. Head departs after getting a solid start.
Commentary.Howout: c Kuldeep Yadav b Hardik Pandya

Commentary.Commentary: Deliberately played in the air! Good length around off, the pace is taken off and Travis Head looks to loft it over mid off. The ball goes off the toe end but clears mid off and they get a couple of runs.
Back of a length around off, Travis Head hangs back and nudges it down toward backward point.

FOUR! Valiant effort from Shubman Gill in the deep but he puts down the catch! Hardik Pandya bangs it in short over leg stump, Travis Head pulls it flat and hard toward deep mid-wicket. Gill runs in from deep square leg and dives forward, getting both hands on it but fumbles and the ball goes through for a boundary as well.
Starts off with a good-length ball around the top of off. Mitchell Marsh stands tall and eases it through the point region for a single.
Powerplay 2! The fielding side can how have up to 4 players outside the inner ring till the 40th over. Also, Hardik Pandya comes into the attack now.
Fuller one on pads, Travis Head tucks this to square leg for no run. A tidy over for India.
Quicker and flatter on middle, Mitchell Marsh pushes this to long on and takes a single.
Fuller and on off, Mitchell Marsh pushes this to short cover.
Tossed up outside off, Mitchell Marsh gets and inside edge that bounces near the stumps.
Turn and bounce on offer as he lands one fractionally short and just outside off, Mitchell Marsh gets beaten on his outside edge.
Fuller and on off, Mitchell Marsh blocks this out.

Fuller around the pads, Travis Head looks to play across the line but gets beaten as the ball has hit his pads. Loud appeal by Siraj but the umpire turns this down and after a lot od deliberation, India opt against the review.
FOUR! Well anticipated and lofted over point for four. Back of a length around leg, Travis Head shuffles to his leg and lofts this over Ravindra Jadeja at point for four.
Short-pitched delivery outside off, Travis Head looks to pull but gets beaten by the bounce on this.
Back of a length over middle, Travis Head looks to push on the off side but gets beaten.
FOUR! On a length around middle, Travis Head slogs this over the short mid-wicket fielder for a boundary. That went like a tracer bullet.
Good length delivery around middle, Travis Head looks to slog but gets an inside edge onto his pads for no run.
Fuller and on off, Mitchell Marsh defends this of the front foot for no run.
Fractionally short and wide of off, Mitchell Marsh cuts this but finds the fielder at cover-point.
Tossed up in middle, Mitchell Marsh pushes this to point.
FOUR! Intentionally hit uppishly over the infield on the off side for four. Fuller outside off, Mitchell Marsh drives this over cover for a boundary.
Fuller one on pads, Travis Head flicks this wide of short fine leg for a single.
SIX! Terrific strike for a maximum. Fuller around middle, Travis Head lofts this over the bowler's head for a maximum right on the sight screen.
On a length around off, Mitchell Marsh defends this to short mid-wicket. Maiden over by Mohammed Siraj.
Back of a length chest high, Mitchell Marsh blocks this out back to the bowler.
Good length delivery around pads, Mitchell Marsh clips this off his pads and tries to take a single but Travis Head refuses the call and rightly so.
Well-directed bouncer, Mitchell Marsh looks to pull but gets beaten.
Back of a length on top of middle, Mitchell Marsh plays the stroke early and gets hit on his thigh pads.
On a length around middle, Mitchell Marsh blocks this out on the on side.
Mohammed Siraj (2-0-17-0) switches ends.
Touch fuller on off, Mitchell Marsh hops on his back foot and drives this wide of Rohit Sharma at extra cover who half-stops this and deflects the ball to long off as the batters take a single.
Short in length on top of off, Mitchell Marsh defends this back to the bowler.
Tossed up around off, Travis Head pushes this just wide off cover-point and steals a single.
Fuller around off, Travis Head cuts this to cover-point.
Floater on middle, Travis Head pushes this to short mid-wicket for no run.
Quicker and wide of off, Travis Head mishits this to short cover.
Axar Patel comes into the attack now.
FOUR! Depth touch for yet another boundary. On a length around pads, Mitchell Marsh just flicks this off his pads for a boundary towards fine leg.
Good length delivery on top of middle, Travis Head taps this near the square on off and takes a quick single. Good running between the wickets by these two.
On a length around off, Travis Head connects the cut shot but finds Ravindra Jadeja at point.
Short and wide of off, Travis Head looks to cut but misses out completely.
SIX! Travis Head gets into the act as well. Fuller one on pads, Travis Head flicks this up and over the infield for a maximum towards the deep square leg fence.
Good length delivery on top of off, Travis Head pushes this to point for no run.
FOUR! That's a cracker for four. Half-volley on off, Mitchell Marsh presents full face of his bat and drills this past the bowler for a boundary towards the long off fence.
Fuller and on off, Mitchell Marsh pushes this to short cover for no run.
Good length delivery wide of off, Mitchell Marsh gets beaten as the ball clips his pads. Loud appeal by Mohammed Siraj but the umpire turns this down.

FOUR! Mitchell Marsh is dealing in boundaries. Pure timing on this for four. On a length around middle, Mitchell Marsh pushes at this but times this perfectly as the ball races past Rohit Sharma at mid on for a boundary.
Leg bye. On a length around pads, Travis Head looks to play across the line but gets a deflection of his pads to point and they take a single.
Full and wide of off, Travis Head drives this well but finds the fielder at mid off.
On a length outside off, slightly slower and nipped back in, Mitchell Marsh gets beaten on his inside edge.
On a length outside off, Mitchell Marsh blocks this out to short cover.
Fuller outside off, Mitchell Marsh hurries into the stroke and has driven this uppishly just in front of mid off.
SIX! Pick-up stroke with effortless ease for a maximum. Fuller and on pads, Mitchell Marsh flicks this way over the fence at deep mid-wicket for the first maximum of this game.
Back of a length outside off, Mitchell Marsh defends this to short cover.
On a length nipping just a fraction in towards the batter, Mitchell Marsh gets beaten and the ball has clipped his front pad. This was going down leg.
Brilliant fielding effort by Virat Kohli saves a certain boundary. On a length angling away from Travis Head, he stands tall and drives this wide of extra cover but Kohli fields well.
Touch fuller on top of off, Mitchell Marsh places this to sweeper cover for a single.
FOUR! Back of a length around middle, Mitchell Marsh uses his height and stands tall as he dismisses this over the short mid-wicket fielder for the second boundary of this over.
Full and wide of off, Mitchell Marsh decides to leave this for the keeper to collect.
FOUR! On a length around pads, Mitchell Marsh stands tall and flicks this over short mid-wicket for a boundary. Mitchell Marsh is off in familiar style.
Fuller one on off, Mitchell Marsh pushes this to cover for no run.
Mohammed Siraj to take the other new ball.
Full and wide of off, Travis Head pushes this to point for no run to end the first over.
FOUR! Glorious drive for four. Travis Head is off the mark and so is Australia. Over-pitched outside off, Travis Head drives this as the ball flies past mid off for the first boundary of the game.
Fuller one around middle, Travis Head guides this on a couple of bounces to point.
Fuller one around off, Travis Head slices this and finds the fielder at point.
Good length delivery outside off angling in towards the batter, Travis Head looks to push through this but misses out on the inside edge.
Mohammad Shami starts bang-on. On a length right on top of off, Travis Head pushes this to mid off.

We are ready for the start of play! The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of India. Mitchell Marsh and Travis Head are set to open the innings for Australia. Mohammad Shami has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

India's skipper, Rohit Sharma says that they were thinking of fielding first and there might be help for the spinners in the heat and they can maximise the conditions. Adds that it is an important game and deciders are always an interesting game and hopefully they can put their best foot forward. Mentions that Australia is a great team and the depth of the side is tested against such quality side. Informs that they are playing with the same team and it is important to give a bit of a run to the players.

Steven Smith, the captain of Australia says they will bat first  as the track looks like dry and it is really hot ao they are looking to post a total. He adds that the series has been fun but this is a crunch gane so it will be fun. He also adds that the team combination is different as David Warner and Ashton Agar come in for Cameron Green who isn't feeling well and Nathan Ellis.

Australia (Playing XI) - Travis Head, Mitchell Marsh, Steven Smith (C), David Warner (In for Cameron Green), Alex Carey (WK), Marnus Labuschagne, Marcus Stoinis, Ashton Agar (In for Nathan Ellis), Sean Abbott, Mitchell Starc, and Adam Zampa.

India (Unchanged Playing XI) - Rohit Sharma (C), Shubman Gill, Virat Kohli, Suryakumar Yadav, KL Rahul (WK), Hardik Pandya, Ravindra Jadeja, Axar Patel, Kuldeep Yadav, Mohammad Shami, and Mohammed Siraj.
TOSS - The two captains are out in the middle and the flip of the coin lands in favor of Australia. They have elected to BAT first.

PITCH REPORT - Sanjay Manjrekar is pitchside and says it is short on one side of the wicket and the straignt boundary is 75 meters. Ajit Agarkar joins him and says that the series has produced generally low scores and there is an even covering of grass but there is some roughness as well. Adds that it might be two-paced in the first innings but will get better for batting as the game goes on.

Australia on the contrary would be buzzing ahead of this game after their brilliant display with the bat, the ball as well as in the field in the last game as they won the second ODI without breaking a sweat. Mitchell Marsh has been sesational in both the ODIs so far and the rate at which he has scored has blown away the Indian bowlers. Mitchell Starc has been impressive as well as he has not let any breathing apace for the Indian batters who have had no answers against him so far. Can the Aussies keep the party going and seal a 2-1 comeback victory over the might Indians? Or will the home side make adjustments and reign supreme? We shall find out. Toss and team news coming up in a bit.

India started off sensationally with a five-wicket victory over the Aussies but the visitors bounced back and in some style as they smashed the hosts in the second ODI by a margin of ten-wickets. The top order woes have been haunting India since long and it can be seen in this series as well. The trouble that the Indian stalwarts have against the left-arm seamer has been well exploited by the likes of Mitchell Starc. If India are to win this series then their top order needs to fire and give the middle order some security from the new ball.

Hello and a very warm welcome to everyone tuning in. We are all set for a thrilling finale to this third and final game of three-match ODI series between India and Australia. MA Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai will be the host for this game. The game promises to be a box-office hit and let's see who clinches the final game and that beautiful silverware that comes with it.
... MATCH DAY ...

We arrive at the last match of a tour that has lasted almost one and a half months with the mighty Australians fighting toe-to-toe with the hosts on Indian shores. Having clinched the Test series 2-1, India will be eager to win the third and decisive ODI at the M. A. Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai to continue their good run at home. They registered a 5-wicket win in the first match but the visitors came roaring back as they demolished the Indian batting and chased down an under-par target with 10 wickets to spare using just 11 overs. The momentum is definitely on the side of the Aussies and they have a golden opportunity to head back home with a trophy thereby sharing the spoils on this tour. India's batting showed early cracks in the first match itself when they lost their first five wickets in no time and needed a 100-run plus partnership between KL Rahul and Ravindra Jadeja to get over the finish line. After losing the toss Rohit Sharma, who returned to the side after missing the first game, was asked to bat first and the hosts lost both their openers inside 5 overs. Suryakumar Yadav's poor run with the bat continues as he was dismissed on a golden duck in two consecutive games with KL Rahul, Hardik Pandya, and Ravindra Jadeja not able to contribute either. Virat Kohli was able to get to a decent start but perished playing across the line once again and Axar Patel looked to carry on his form from the Test series but ran out of partners at the other end. Mohammad Shami and Mohammed Siraj did the bulk of the damage in the first match but with a low target to defend in the previous tie, all the bowlers were carted around the ground and went wicketless. Australia are yet to deploy David Warner who seems to be still recovering from his elbow injury but his unavailability has not been noticed as Mitchell Marsh has welcomed the opener's role with open arms. He has now scored quickfire half-centuries in both games, remaining unbeaten last time around with his opening partner Travis Head who also managed to score a fifty. Steven Smith, Marnus Labuschagne, and Cameron Green got a bit of time at the wicket in the first game but could not play longer innings and were not required in the second match. Australia's success was heavily dependent on Mitchell Starc who claimed his ninth ODI five-wicket haul and once again caused havoc among the Indian batters. They read the pitch perfectly and unlike India, went with an extra pace-bowling option with Nathan Ellis and Sean Abbott claiming the remaining five wickets. With the pitch at this venue more conducive to spin, we could see India stick with their extra spinning options and Australia could bring in Ashton Agar or Glenn Maxwell if he is fit enough to play. India will look to get some southpaws in their top order which is predominantly right-handed to negotiate the inward movement from Mitchell Starc and this could make way for Ishan Kishan in the lineup. After two low-scoring affairs, the fans will be eager for a run-fest but this ground is not known for massive scores and the weather will also be quite hot and humid. With both teams not scheduled to play an ODI till after the Test Championship final midway through the year, they will need to make the most of this game in light of their World Cup preparations. Will India overcome the disappointment of the drubbing they faced in their last match? Or will Australia continue their winning momentum and seal the series? We will find out soon.
